title: The farewell pilgrimage
hookLine: the Prophet ﷺ performs his one Hajj with a vast crowd

lines: PILGRIMS AS FAR AS THE EYE COULD SEE.
cards: A photo of the Hajj looks like water moving: a sea of people around the Ka'ba, the men in the same two plain white cloths. Those rites go back to one journey.
In the tenth year after the hijra, the Prophet ﷺ announced he was going to Mecca for the pilgrimage. It was the only Hajj he made after leaving Mecca, and word spread fast.
People came from all over Arabia to go with him, so many that, the reports say, you could look to your right and left, in front and behind, and see only pilgrims.

teach.b: Much of what's known comes from one long hadith in Sahih Muslim, told by a companion named Jabir, who walks through the pilgrimage step by step, almost like a travel diary.
At a place outside Medina, the Prophet put on ihram, the state of the pilgrim; for the men, that meant two unstitched white cloths.
A king and a shepherd look exactly the same in them.

Then he began the talbiyah, and the crowd called it with him: labbayk, Allahumma, labbayk. Here I am, O God, here I am. Labbayk is the answer you give when someone calls your name and you come running.
Jabir describes him circling the Ka'ba, walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah, standing at Arafah, throwing stones at Mina.
Along the way, he said something that explains why Muslims still perform Hajj in almost exactly these steps: take your rites from me, for I may not make the pilgrimage again after this year.
He was teaching by doing, and he seems to have known it was the last chance. That's why it's called the farewell pilgrimage.

Today the men still wear the same two white cloths; women wear modest clothing, which may be white as well. And the call is the same one Jabir heard: here I am. All in white, all saying the same thing, all equal.

how: Muslims able to afford it and physically able are required to make the Hajj once in their lives; pilgrims enter ihram, men in two white unstitched cloths, and follow the rites the Prophet performed on his farewell pilgrimage, calling the talbiyah as they go.

o: God is greatest, the opening of the prayer
peace be upon you, a pilgrim's greeting
here I am, the reply when God calls you

p: told the journey step by step

games.q: you're leading a vast crowd of pilgrims, and you may not come back. how do you teach the rites?
o: write them down and send the list to every tribe.
do them in front of everyone and say: take your rites from me.
leave it to each tribe's custom.
games.why: he taught by doing: take your rites from me, for I may not make the pilgrimage again after this year. Muslims still follow those steps.

practice: Close your eyes if you like and see the plain: a huge crowd, every person dressed the same, so you can't tell who's rich, who's well-known, who's in charge.
Now put yourself in it, in the same plain cloth, with nothing that marks you out, and notice what that feels like: lighter, maybe, or strange.
If you pray, you can whisper the pilgrim's words, here I am; if you don't, just rest in the crowd.

wordCard.voice: Labbayk. The answer pilgrims called back to God during the Prophet's one Hajj, made with a vast crowd, not long before he died. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: here I am, at your service. the first word of the talbiyah, called by pilgrims.

carryVoice: Your line: all in white. No one in that crowd stood out above anyone else. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 1218 (Jabir's account of the Prophet's Hajj)
